subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
subtype: Approach: saving evidence before anything is deleted [Action]
passage: Tuesday, late. I took screenshots of everything before it could vanish: the messages, the names of who sent them, the dates and times. I saved the links, too. Then I put it all in one private folder and wrote a list on paper, in order: what, who, when. I did not reply to anyone, though I wanted to. Amma saw me at the desk and read over my shoulder, and she sat down and put her hand over mine. She said, “This is not your fault.” She said we'd take the folder to Urmila ma'am at school first thing, and she rang to ask if we could come at eight. I still feel shaky, but I'm not carrying it by myself tonight. — Santosh

qa.q: Where did Santosh keep the screenshots?
How does Santosh feel at the end of the entry?
qa.a: Shaky but a little steadier: the evidence is saved and Amma is on Santosh's side.

qa.q: What else could Santosh do to protect the proof, and why?
qa.a: Keep a second copy somewhere safe and delete nothing, since deleted messages cannot be checked later.

qa.q: How does the folder look to Urmila ma'am?
qa.a: Urmila ma'am gets real dates and names instead of only a story, so the school can act through its own process.

grounding: A student saves screenshots showing messages, names and dates, so that adults, the school or police can act on real proof.

subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
subtype: Approach: saving evidence before anything is deleted [Action]
passage:
In Moga, where half the town knows whose son you are, the fake profile spread fast: a page using Harish's photo, posting mocking lines about his stammer. His sister Gurleen found it first, on Sunday afternoon.
“Don't report it yet,” she said. “If it disappears, there's no proof.”
Harish sat on the charpai with her phone and his, hands unsteady. He took a screenshot of the profile page, then of each post, making sure the account name and date showed at the top. He copied the profile's link into a note. Twelve screenshots in all. Gurleen made a locked folder on his phone, and they moved everything there.
That evening they showed Bauji. He scrolled through every picture without a word, then said, “Tomorrow, the principal. If the school can't stop it, the police station. With this, they'll have to listen.”

qa.q: How many screenshots did Harish take?
What do Harish's unsteady hands suggest?
qa.a: They suggest he was upset and nervous, even while carefully collecting the proof.

qa.q: What else could Harish's family do if the page keeps posting?
qa.a: Keep adding dated screenshots to the locked folder and also report the page through the app, so every new post is on record.

qa.q: How does the plan look to Bauji?
qa.a: Bauji sees solid proof in hand, which makes him confident the principal, or the police if needed, will have to act.

grounding: Shows a student screenshotting a fake profile's posts with names and dates, saving the link, and keeping it in a locked folder so adults can act on proof.
